title: Wave Particle Duality
definition: Wave-particle duality is the concept in quantum mechanics that every particle exhibits properties of both waves and particles.

difficulty_levels.beginner: Imagine a lighthouse sending out light beams. The light is both a wave — spreading out in all directions — and a particle — individual photons hitting your eye. Until you look, light exists in all possibilities simultaneously. This is wave-particle duality.
difficulty_levels.intermediate: Wave-particle duality is a foundational concept in quantum mechanics, stating that particles can exist in multiple states simultaneously until observed. This is demonstrated by phenomena such as the double-slit experiment.
difficulty_levels.expert: Wave-particle duality challenges our classical understanding of reality. It highlights the probabilistic nature of quantum mechanics and the non-locality of quantum systems. This has significant implications for the nature of consciousness and the measurement problem.

extra_fields.insight: Reality is not binary. It exists in multiple states simultaneously until observed, challenging our classical notions of certainty and separation.
